value.claim: First-depositor inflation/griefing: a direct token transfer to an empty vault raises share price so subsequent deposits below the threshold mint 0 shares, with the 3-arg deposit's minSharesOut=0 also passing.
value.support_reason: Vault inherits Solady ERC4626 with no virtual-share/dead-share offset and no initial dead-share mint in initialize (Vault.sol:51-71); deposit (Vault.sol:78-87) and deposit(assets,to,minSharesOut) (Vault.sol:94-103) delegate to super.deposit, which prices shares from totalAssets()/totalSupply() where totalAssets is token balanceOf(this) (Solady ERC4626). A direct ERC20 transfer to the empty vault inflates the price; a deposit below that price yields 0 shares. minSharesOut in the 3-arg overload provides no protection because convertToShares returns 0 in the same state, so the `shares < minSharesOut` check at Vault.sol:102 passes with 0.
preconditions: Vault is freshly deployed with zero shares/totalSupply (first deposit not yet made)
Attacker (or anyone, permissionless) transfers depositToken directly to the vault address before the intended first deposit
Victim deposits an amount smaller than the direct-transfer amount, or uses the 3-arg deposit with convertToShares-derived minSharesOut (which is 0)
missing_evidence: test showing deposit-receipt loss under the async redeem path: confirm startRedeem/finishRedeem cannot recover zero-share deposit assets since no shares were minted
show that the griefed deposit assets are not recoverable by anyone including the vault owner (i.e. not just temporarily stranded)

The sentinel DEFAULT_VAULT_IMPLEMENTATION_FLAG is never written to allowlistedVaultImpl (allowlistVaultImpl CoreLib.sol:153-155 is only called with real impls, and Core.sol:213 explicitly rejects the flag) and is not self.vaultImpl (Core.sol:173-178 rejects the flag). value.claim: Vault is vulnerable to inflation/donation attack because the first depositor can mint 1 wei of shares, donate assets, and cause later depositors to receive 0 shares.
value.support_reason: Solady ERC4626 (virtual shares/assets offset: decimalsOffset virtual shares and 1 virtual asset) make the classic 1-wei/1-share donation attack profitless; the report itself concedes the attacker must donate 2x the victim deposit to break even, which is a no-gain griefing scenario, not asset theft. Also, `deposit(assets,to)` path has no protection claim check omitted, but the 3-arg overload at src/Vault.sol:94 with minSharesOut exists and the docs steer users to it (src/Vault.sol:89-93, docs at src/Vault.sol:28 warn against donations).

value.claim: SlashingHandler.handleSlashing reverts for fee-on-transfer tokens because it transfers `amount` from its own balance after receiving `amount - fee`.
value.support_reason: handleSlashing pulls `amount` via safeTransferFrom (L56) then pushes `amount` to address(0) (L58) from its own balance; for a fee-on-transfer token the received balance is less than `amount`, so the outgoing transfer/balance check fails. No check elsewhere blocks this path; Vault.slashAssets (Vault.sol:193-205) simply forwards the transferAmount, and the README explicitly puts fee-on-transfer tokens in scope. The root cause is the unsupported-asset handling; note a partial workaround: if the handler only holds exactly the received amount, transfer of `amount` reverts (DoS on slashing), which matches the claim.
preconditions: asset allowlisted with a SlashingHandler and token is fee-on-transfer (in scope per README)
missing_evidence: demonstration that the revert occurs with a concrete fee-on-transfer token and a non-zero pre-existing handler balance or not (distinguish simple revert vs. stuck funds)

note this is essentially the ineligible bot M-1 fee-on-transfer accounting issue for the same line

value.claim: DSS can burn up to the high global `hookCallGasLimit` inside its hook (e.g. `unregistrationHook`) with `ignoreFailure: true`, forcing the operator to overpay gas, since one global `hookCallGasLimit` is shared across all DSSes
value.support_reason: A single storage-wide `self.hookCallGasLimit` (CoreLib.sol:62-64) is passed into every hook call (e.g. Operator.sol:78-86, 124-132, 162-170, 194-202; SlasherLib.sol:113-123, 142-150, 159-167). `HookLib.callHook` (48-64) forwards exactly that gas limit to the DSS via `performLowLevelCallAndLimitReturnData`, and with `ignoreFailure: true` a failure does not revert — the DSS hook can unconditionally consume up to the forwarded gas. No per-DSS or per-hook cap exists; the operator pays the gas.

value.claim: Slashed amount is computed from totalAssets at request time and stored unchanged until finalization; for tokens with balance changes outside transfers (e.g. rebasing stETH), the fixed share/token amount can represent a larger underlying value at finalize time, over-slashing the vault.
value.support_reason: SlasherLib.fetchEarmarkedStakes (SlasherLib.sol:86-90) fixes earmarkedStakes at request time via mulDiv(percentage, totalAssets(), MAX). Core.requestSlashing (Core.sol:229) stores this into QueuedSlashing; finalizeSlashing (SlasherLib.sol:126-139) reuses the stored earmarkedStakes[i] and passes it to Vault.slashAssets, which only clamps to current totalAssets (Vault.sol:198). Nothing recomputes the amount at finalize time, so a balance-affecting change (rebasing) in between alters the value the fixed amount represents. Vault uses Solady ERC4626 totalAssets() = token balanceOf(vault), consistent with the scenario.
preconditions: Vault underlying token is a rebasing/balance-change-outside-transfer token in scope (e.g. stETH)
Vault's token balance (totalAssets) increases via rebase during the SLASHING_VETO_WINDOW
DSS requests slashing, does not get vetoed
finalizeSlashing executed after veto window
